The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

description: Our Open Studio program invites participants to create in the museum's art studio, where art becomes a tool for reflection, expression, and connection. title: Louisa's Garden | Exhibition
description: Louisa's Garden, the Wylie House Museum's latest exhibition, explores the way the eldest daughter of an IU professor was brave, complex, and is still cherished today. For Louisa's Garden, Graduate Curatorship student Maddie Guy selected five ensembles from the Elizabeth Sage Historic Costume Collection. These five nineteenth century ensembles, though not directly related to Louisa Wylie Boisen (1839–1930), were carefully chosen to represent aspects of her life including Education, Motherhood, Travel, Religion, and Gardening.Wylie House hours: Friday–Saturday, 10am–4pm. Free, guided tours begin on the hour every hour, with the last one beginning at 3pm. The museum is closed on major holidays, IU commencement weekend, and during Indiana University breaks. Please contact the museum to arrange group tours with more than eight people.  For more information about The Sage Collection, please visit their webpage. (https://eskenazi.indiana.edu/about/centers-collections/sage-collection/index.html)  For more information about Wylie House Museum (https://libraries.indiana.edu/wylie-house-museum) visit their website.
source: Architecture + Design, IU Bloomington Libraries, IU Eskenazi School of Art

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Exhibition Opening Reception for The Photographic Reflex: The Lee Marks and John C. DePrez Jr. Collection
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
description: Thursday, September 10, 20264–6 p.m. Opening reception  Hors d'oeuvres and cash bar (4–6 p.m.)  First floor atrium  About The Photographic Reflex: The Lee Marks and John C. DePrez Jr. Collection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/exhibitions/upcoming/_feature-exhibitions/2026-08-29-photographic-reflex-marks-deprez.html):  Spanning more than 150 years, The Photographic Reflex celebrates a transformative gift to the IU Eskenazi Museum of Art from collectors Lee Marks and John C. DePrez Jr. The exhibition features more than one hundred photographs by eighty artists, highlighting the breadth, power, and enduring impact of photographic expression.  Photographs dating from 1856 to 2017 reveal photography's dual role as both a tool for documentation and a vehicle for artistic exploration. Organized into five thematic sections—Play of Light, Industrial Eye, Photographic Figure, Witness to Conflict, and Impressed by Nature's Hand—the exhibition examines how photographers across disciplines have communicated ideas, recorded history, and shaped visual culture.  The exhibition includes works by many of the most influential figures in the medium, from Berenice Abbott, Alfred Stieglitz, Edward Steichen, and Henri Cartier-Bresson to contemporary artists such as Edward Burtynsky, Abelardo Morell, Susan Derges, and Vik Muniz.  A richly illustrated exhibition catalogue, featuring an interview with the collectors, will accompany The Photographic Reflex and will be available for purchase through the museum's Newkirk Café and Gift Shop.
source: Architecture + Design, Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Eskenazi School of Art

title: Materialism Reading Group
location: Redbud Books, 408 W Kirkwood Ave, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
A long-term, hybrid in-person and online reading group in memory of our beloved friend, Joshua Clover inspired by Joshua’s understanding of communism, and social transformation. 

Our itinerary begins with Riot Strike Riot (Clover) and works backward through Chaos and Governance in the Modern World System (Arrighi and silver ), The Eclipse And Re-emergence Of The Communist Movement(Dauvé and Martin), The Arcana Of Reproduction (Fortunati, Trans Austin and Colantuono), Notes On Dialectics (James), Capital V I (Marx, Trans Reitter or Fowkes) and then returns to the present for The Future of Revolution (Bernes). 

If people agree the group will be run as a discussion by rotating facilitators. It could last 18 months or so.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

We will move beyond the syllabus to show you how to form a team, align with faculty expertise, and submit a winning bid.What we will cover:The Matchmaking Strategy: Using our internal interest lists to pair student technical skills with faculty subject-matter expertise.    The Bidding Mechanics: A step-by-step guide to the project menu and the requirements for faculty-led submissions.    The 3-Credit Standard: Why we are standardizing the Lab experience to ensure professional parity and academic rigor. description: Designed for K-12 students and their families, this event offers a fun and flexible way to spark creativity and connect with each other. All ages and experience levels are welcome!  Come and go at your own pace. We recommend planning for at least an hour to explore the gallery and make art.  Start in the Art Studio inside the Kimberly and John Simpson Center for Education on the museum's 2nd floor to pick up your Gallery Challenge. title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop
description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.  


It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.  


Instructions:  


Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session 


If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop. 


If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu. 


All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all IU students and other members of the Indiana University community. 


Hosted by: Office for Sexual Violence Prevention and Victim Advocacy

Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12491857

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: WKU Fly Fishing Montana September 2026
description:
AND
September 20 –  September 25  
Join WKU and experience fly fishing on world-renowned
waters which contain several trout species and
other fish such as mountain whitefish, northern
pikeminnow, and pike. Guides typically take
participants on one or more of the following
rivers: Blackfoot, Clark Fork, Bitterroot. 
No prior fly-fishing experience is required.
This program is designed to meet the
needs of the complete beginner and ‘experts’
alike; whatever an expert is. All fishing will be
from drift boats or rafts. Being able to cast a
flyrod is certainly helpful, but not a requirement
as on-the-river instruction is readily available.
WKU has successfully offered this program since
2012 to participants with a wide range of abilities
(from no prior experience to being a fly-fishing
guide).

title: Bike Project Open Hours
description:
The Community Bike Project is a Bloomington-based organization that focuses on providing bike transportation to the people of the city. We focus on teaching bicycle maintenence in order to ensure that bikes on the streets stay on the streets. Here is what we do: Community Bike Project Front Door



    * bikes for sale: we sell gently used bikes at bargain prices

    * earn-a-bike program: participants can receive a bicycle after volunteering their time in our shop

    * advocacy: we support alternative forms of transportation; we support the reuse and recycling of bicycles

    * workshops & classes: we offer unique bike maintence workshops and classes for children and adults

    * open shop: we make our tools available to the public

The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.  


It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.

Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session 


If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop. 


If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Your DC Moment | Dinner with Ambassador and Professor Lee Feinstein
description: Stop studying global leadership and start practicing it. Join Ambassador and Professor Lee Feinstein, our D.C. Program Academic Director, for an exclusive working dinner and strategy session for the Spring 2027 D.C. Global Policy Program.  This intimate dinner is for students interested in the Hamilton Lugar Spring 2027 residency. It's a working dinner and a peek at what a global career actually feels like before you step into it.Why you should attend:Sit at the Table: Engage with leaders who have shaped global policy and international careers.    Alumni Insights: Hear from a panel of D.C. Program alumni regarding their on-the-ground experiences.    Professional Roadmap: Get a technical walkthrough of the Spring 2027 cycle, including the January 12 – May 2 residency dates.    The Logistics Bridge: Understand how the IU Capital Campus housing works and how the classes work for undergrads, grad, and PhD students.    The Strategy Session AgendaI. The Practitioner Perspective: A briefing from Ambassador Lee Feinstein on D.C. professional realities and "tradecraft" skills.    II. The Roadmap: A deep dive into the October 15 deadline, interview sprints (Oct 26–28), and the mandatory December 12 orientation.    III. Housing & Classes: Guidance on the Capital Campus residency and the academic courses offered in D.C.    IV. Ground Game: Peer-to-peer breakouts and alumni panel discussion on commuting, and professional life in DC.    Biography: Ambassador & Professor Lee Feinstein  Ambassador Lee Feinstein is a Senior Managing Director and the President of McLarty Associates. He previously served as the U.S. Ambassador to the Republic of Poland and held senior positions at the Department of State, including Principal Deputy Director and a Member of the Policy Planning Staff. He was the Founding Dean of the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies at Indiana University from 2014 to 2022. Ambassador Feinstein is a member of the Council on Foreign Relations and the American Academy of Diplomacy, and holds a JD from Georgetown University Law Center.   Can't make the full hour? No problem. This is a come-and-go strategy session designed to fit your Thursday schedule.

title: Materialism Reading Group
location: Redbud Books, 408 W Kirkwood Ave, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
A long-term, hybrid in-person and online reading group in memory of our beloved friend, Joshua Clover inspired by Joshua’s understanding of communism, and social transformation. 

Our itinerary begins with Riot Strike Riot (Clover) and works backward through Chaos and Governance in the Modern World System (Arrighi and silver ), The Eclipse And Re-emergence Of The Communist Movement(Dauvé and Martin), The Arcana Of Reproduction (Fortunati, Trans Austin and Colantuono), Notes On Dialectics (James), Capital V I (Marx, Trans Reitter or Fowkes) and then returns to the present for The Future of Revolution (Bernes). 

If people agree the group will be run as a discussion by rotating facilitators. It could last 18 months or so.

Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (https://go.iu.edu/america-250), a months-long civic festival offering our state expansive programming, exhibits, and events to honor our country's past while looking toward our shared future through common experiences for our campus and community.
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop
description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.  


It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.  


Instructions:  


Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session 


If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop. 


If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu. 


All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all IU students and other members of the Indiana University community. 


Hosted by: Office for Sexual Violence Prevention and Victim Advocacy

Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12491861

description:

    * bikes for sale: we sell gently used bikes at bargain prices

    * earn-a-bike program: participants can receive a bicycle after volunteering their time in our shop

    * advocacy: we support alternative forms of transportation; we support the reuse and recycling of bicycles

    * open shop: we make our tools available to the public

title: Arts Mile
description:
Experience downtown Bloomington’s vibrant Arts Mile as select galleries showcase evolving live and virtual exhibits.

EVERY. FIRST. FRIDAY. Experience an exciting night of the arts as fourteen distinct galleries stay open late to host special exhibits and serve refreshments from 5-8pm.

Stroll the vibrant arts scene along the sensational art mile and experience amazing art by renowned local, regional, and international artists. Discover delightful surprises, inspiration, festivities, and original works of art for purchase. Explore each distinctive gallery in-person or online all year long at your own pace.

Click here to learn more https://www.gallerywalkbloomington.com/

title: Arts Village
description:
Friday October 2nd from 6PM – 10PM
Saturday October 3rd from 6PM – 10PM
Kirkwood on the Square (Between College Ave and Walnut)
The Arts Village is where creativity comes to life during the festival weekend. Wander through a vibrant evening atmosphere filled with live art demonstrations, interactive activities, local and regional artists, and a Night Bazaar celebrating handmade work, creativity, and community. Discover new artists, try your hand at creative experiences, and enjoy the energy of the festival after dark. 
During the festival-wide break at 8:30 PM Friday evening, enjoy a special Taste of the IU Drumline bringing rhythm and excitement to the heart of downtown. Then on Saturday evening, the 2026 Parade returns, lighting up the streets with music, movement, and celebration once again. 
The Arts Village is alive from 6 PM – 10 PM on Friday, October 2nd and Saturday, October 3rd, 2026. This is a free event to attend. Donations are appreciated and help support the mission of the Lotus Education and Arts Foundation. 
Interested in participating as an artist? Email KP at associatedirector@lotusfest.org.

title: Arts Camp
description:
Saturday, October 3
12:00 PM – 4:00 PM
The annual Lotus Arts Camp is back..this time on the Square! Join us on Saturday, October 3, 2026, from 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM for an afternoon of free, family-friendly crafts, activities, and community fun in the heart of downtown. 
Families are invited to explore hands-on activities, connect with local organizations, and celebrate creativity together. Admission is free and all are welcome. 
Interested in partnering with the Arts Camp?
Community partners are invited to host a hands-on craft, activity, or interactive experience for kids and families. Or contact our production manager – Chaz Mottinger at productionmanager@lotusfest.org.

title: Parade Through the Lights
description:
Date: October 3rd
Time: 8:30 PM
Location: Courthouse Square
As the sun sets and the lanterns begin to glow, the Lotus Festival Parade invites the community to step into a living work of art. Led by the spirit of Lotus and brought to life through music, dance, movement, and imagination, this illuminated procession transforms downtown into a celebration of connection and creativity.
Guided by the warm light of the Trail of Luminaria, participants and spectators alike will journey together through a night filled with rhythm, color, and wonder. From handmade lanterns to spontaneous joy, every light and every person becomes part of the story. 
All are welcome. All are needed. Whether you dance, carry a lantern, create art, volunteer, or simply walk beside us, your presence helps brighten the path forward. 
Interested in joining the effort, volunteering, or partnering?
Email KP at associatedirector@lotusfest.org and share your light.

title: Paula Poundstone
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater,114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Iconic comedian Paula Poundstone is known for her smart, observational humor and a spontaneous wit that has become the stuff of legend. She regularly plays theaters across the country, hosts a weekly comedy podcast, Nobody Listens to Paula Poundstone, and is a regular panelist on NPR’s Wait, Wait… Don’t Tell Me. She also voiced the character ‘Forgetter Paula’ in the feature films Inside Out and Inside Out 2.

Paula has starred in several HBO specials, including Cats, Cops and Stuff, which nabbed a cable ACE award for Best Comedy Special. She was the first female comic to host the White House Correspondents Dinner. She filmed live coverage of the 1992 Democratic and Republican National Conventions and the Presidential Inaugural for The Tonight Show with Jay Leno and at the 93rd Emmy Awards. Paula has starred in two television series, both entitled The Paula Poundstone Show.

Paula’s second book, The Totally Unscientific Study of the Search for Human Happiness, was one of eight semi-finalists for the Thurber Prize for American Humor; the audiobook was one of five finalists for the AUDIE award for Audiobook of the Year.

Paula has released five albums and is featured in several documentaries and compendiums noting influential comedians of our time.

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

description: Get ready to experience a revival! Presented by Awakening Events, Zach Williams' Revival Nights Tour has an energy this fall that's a little gritty, a lot louder, and always real. Singer/Songwriter Christian Hohn opens the night with new music that tells his story of faith in way that suits this tour's theme of everyday life, struggle, and redemption.     Come as you are and experience the transforming power of music, worship and community. A limited number of Revival Nights VIP tickets offer best seating, early merch shopping, and a Meet & Greet with photo opportunity with Zach Williams. Grab your seats before they're gone!

title: Chicago Farmer & The Fieldnotes with special guest The Hammer and The Hatchet
location: Brown County Playhouse, 70 S. Van Buren St, Nashville, IN, 47448, United States
description:
“Chicago Farmer has his finger on the modern Roots pulse with a display of gritty Country Rock and Folk from the gut amid a Folksingers mesh of lyrical humor and problems with a groove.” – The Alternate Root 
“It’s apparent Chicago Farmer has a refreshingly firm grip on where he comes from. The songs are covered to the elbows in dirt from the fields and smell of the sweaty factory floors. If the Midwest is looking for a voice, the search is over.” – No Depression 
“Chicago Farmer represents the best qualities of Midwestern U.S.A. His lyrics, his stories and his heart are true. He’ll give you that feeling of ‘going home’. He’ll make you want to say all those things you’ve been meaning to say but were too afraid. At the same time his songs can make you ask yourself some deep questions. His songs give you hope. If you didn’t know him I believe just his voice would make you believe every word he says. Definitely one of my favorite singers out there today.” – Pokey LaFarge 
With special guest The Hammer and The Hatchet

title: Hotel California – The Original Eagles Tribute
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater,114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
For over three decades now HOTEL CALIFORNIA have been recreating the legendary sound of The Eagles, and thrilling audiences all over the world. From the quintessential Eagles anthem “Hotel California” thru “Take It Easy”, “Lyin’ Eyes”, “Take It to the Limit”, “Peaceful Easy Feeling”, “One of These Nights”, “Dirty Laundry”, “Already Gone”, “The Long Run”, “Life In the Fast Lane” and “Desperado”, they have evolved into a masterful celebration of The Eagles’ music.

The band set the bar in 1986, and they’ve remained the industry leading substitute for The Eagles ever since. Playing to huge outdoor and arena audiences, sharing bills with some of rock’s legends, and going places no tribute band has gone before. A long run by any measure, but it begs the question – what makes HOTEL CALIFORNIA so special?

Simply put, incredible lead vocal similarity, intensely accurate instrumental work, soaring harmonies, and top-flight live performances, just for starters. These are the band’s hallmarks, and the foundation on which their reputation has been built. With over a century of collective professional experience in the band today, they’re still going stronger than ever!

If you love The Eagles, then welcome to the HOTEL CALIFORNIA – you’ve just found the next-best thing.

title: 2026 Conference on Global Indigenous Studies (CGIS)
description: CGIS 2026 is a transdisciplinary event that will bring together national and international scholars, educators, practitioners, students, policy makers, activists, academic institutions, Indigenous organizations, grassroots organizations, governmental and non-governmental organizations. The participants in this conference will be involved in a local and global dialogue and exchange of ideas, research, and experiences on the themes of the event.  Across the globe, ethnic minorities and Indigenous communities have consistently strived to protect their rich cultural heritages and linguistic nuances from the influences of colonial powers, expanding nation-states, and the homogenizing impact of globalization. This collective effort is increasingly recognized, highlighted by the initiation of UNESCO's "Indigenous Languages Decade" (2022-2032) (https://www.unesco.org/en/decades/indigenous-languages/community/adhocgroups). title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: David Cross
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater,114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Emmy Award winner and two-time Grammy Award nominee David Cross is an acclaimed comedian, actor, writer, and producer whose work has left an impactful mark on television, film, and stand-up comedy. He is best known as the co-creator and star of the influential HBO sketch series Mr. Show with Bob and David, and for his iconic role of Tobias Fünke on the Emmy Award-winning series Arrested Development. Cross was also part of the ensemble cast of The Ben Stiller Show, earning an Emmy Award for writing early in his career.

Cross has been performing stand-up comedy for over 40 years, and has released numerous critically acclaimed specials and albums including Making America Great Again! for Netflix, Oh Come On, I’m From The Future, and The Pride Is Back, which was highlighted by Rolling Stone as one of the 25 most important stand-up specials of all time, among multiple others. His comedy albums have earned multiple Grammy nominations, and his international tours have taken him to theatres around the globe. He currently has a residency at Union Hall in NYC through April 2026, and has solidified his reputation as one of the most inventive and fearless voices in comedy.

His latest stand-up special, The End Of The Beginning Of The End, premieres April 7th exclusively on YouTube with 800 Pound Gorilla Media and produced by YMH Studios. Filmed at the legendary 40 Watt Club in Athens, Georgia, Cross dives into New York living, unconventional takes on history, an absurd massage encounter and today’s struggles of being a woman.

On screen, Cross has appeared in a wide range of television projects, including the HBO Max miniseries Station Eleven, Netflix’s The Umbrella Academy, Genius: Aretha, and Goliath. His film credits include Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, Ghost World, Sorry to Bother You, Kill Your Darlings, Alvin and the Chipmunks, She’s the Man, Men in Black, The Post, the 2025 theatrically released comedy Oh, Hi!, and most recently starred and executive produced the indie feature Lucy Shulman, as well as NYTW’s Tartuffe this past winter opposite Matthew Broderick. He has also lent his voice to numerous animated films, including the Kung Fu Panda franchise, Megamind, Next Gen, and Curious George.

Cross is a prolific creator and storyteller both here and abroad. He wrote, created and starred in The Increasingly Poor Decisions of Todd Margaret, a co-production between IFC in the states and Channel 4 in the UK, wrote, directed, and produced, Bliss for Sky TV also in the UK, as well as writing and directing the independent feature Hits, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. He is also the co-author of the book Hollywood Said No!, written with Bob Odenkirk and Brian Posehn as well as the NY Times bestselling author of, I Drink For A Reason. Cross most recently reunited with Odenkirk for the documentary Bob and David Climb Machu Picchu.

David Cross currently resides in Brooklyn, New York.
For more information, please visit https://officialdavidcross.com/ https://officialdavidcross.com/

location: Wells Screening Room (ground floor, within Media Services)

title: Annie
location: Waldron Arts Center,112 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Annie” on stage December 10th - January 3rd at the Waldron Auditorium.

Discover the magic of Annie, the iconic Broadway musical that has captured hearts for generations! The timeless tale of Little Orphan Annie follows a tenacious young girl whose unbreakable optimism leads her on an unforgettable journey from a New York City orphanage to a place she can finally call home. Featuring one of Broadway’s most memorable scores, including “It’s the Hard-Knock Life,” “Easy Street,” “N.Y.C.” and the endlessly-uplifting “Tomorrow,” Annie is a delightful theatrical experience for the entire family. Fun for all ages!

See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/ https://seeconstellation.org/kids/annie/

title: The ConstelLate Show: Holiday Special
location: 112 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “The ConstelLate Show: Holiday Special ” on stage December 17 - 27, 2026 at the Waldron Auditorium.

The ConstelLate Show is Constellation’s very own late-night holiday special—part talk show, part variety show, and completely one-of-a-kind. Running throughout the holidays with brand-new guests each night, this festive evening brings together local luminaries, performers, and personalities. Each episode features interviews, games, live music, comedy, surprise talents, and a few unexpected twists. Complete with cameras and live monitors, audiences won’t just watch the show—they’ll feel like they’re part of the broadcast. It’s joyful, it’s unpredictable, and it’s the most Constellation way imaginable to celebrate the season.

title: An Enemy of the People
location: 112 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “An Enemy of the People” on stage February 4th-21st at the Waldron Auditorium.


This Tony-nominated adaptation of Henrik Ibsen’s masterpiece follows a small-town doctor who discovers a catastrophe that risks the lives of everyone in town. After raising the alarm, he is shaken to his core as those in power, including his own brother, not only try to silence him—they try to destroy him.

title: An Enemy of the People
location: 112 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Mojo & Jimmy: The Totally Awesome Magic Show” on stage March 26th- April 11th at the Waldron Auditorium.


Join Mojo the Monkey and his surprising sidekick Jimmy the Tomato for a jungle adventure packed with laughs and mind-blowing magic. In a world where the bananas are magical and the magic is bananas, everything changes when their beloved tree suddenly stops producing fruit. These two unlikely heroes must step up and pull off their most spectacular tricks yet to save the day. Bursting with big laughs, astonishing illusions, and interactive moments for the whole family, Mojo & Jimmy: The Totally Awesome Magic Show is a joyful celebration of friendship, imagination, and the power of working together. Fun for all ages!


At the PB&J Cafe: Dinner Theater for Kids, young theatergoers will enjoy a meal during the performance and leave with autographs from their favorite characters.


See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/mojo-and-jimmy/ https://seeconstellation.org/kids/mojo-and-jimmy/

title: The Cottage
location: 112 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “The Cottage ” on stage May 13thth- May 30th at the Waldron Auditorium.

When Sylvia decides to expose her latest affair to her husband—and her lover’s wife—an idyllic English countryside getaway turns into a wildly improper disaster. As lovers and spouses collide under one roof, what begins as a scandal quickly spirals into a cascade of outrageous twists, romantic entanglements, and deliciously bad decisions. From the writer of the smash-hit stage adaptation of Clue, The Cottage is a fast-paced farce that delivers big laughs, bold antics, and a giant dose of high-society mischief.

See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/mainstage/the-cottage/ https://seeconstellation.org/mainstage/the-cottage/
